scope: Versioned text-bank baseline across nine languages, with separate General American and Standard Southern British banks. Targeted literature and stimulus-list searches, not an exhaustive systematic review.

ownerTrainingContract.primaryUnit: One specified sound contrast, selected dialect, two word pools and explicit compatible contexts.
ownerTrainingContract.primaryTask: Audio-only category ABX: A and B demonstrate the contrasting categories. X is a different lexical item from one category. The learner chooses the matching sound category.
ownerTrainingContract.textVisibility: No orthography, translation or IPA in the learner trial until optional hints or post-answer reveal. Text is intentionally visible in this owner review.
ownerTrainingContract.wordSelection: Pool membership is independent of minimal-pair linkage. A/B references can be selected from compatible pools; arbitrary Cartesian combinations are not automatically minimal pairs or valid trials. X must differ lexically and in intended whole-word pronunciation from both reference words; homophones with different spellings are not distinct auditory examples.
ownerTrainingContract.voiceSelection: Each approved word should eventually have several independently audited voices and takes. Category, A/B position and speaker must not predict each other. Never reuse an identical recording as the matching X. Hold out both words and voices when evaluating transfer.
ownerTrainingContract.secondaryTask: Optional explicit word identification remains separate; no decision that one method is universally superior.
reviewSequence: Review each category's words, intended IPA, senses and target positions; record missing words and errors.
Only after owner text review, prepare audio candidates.
Audit every word-by-voice recording for lexical identity, target sound, dialect and naturalness before training use. Synthetic checks alone cannot establish correct pronunciation.
ownerTrainingContract.currentImplementationBoundary: This change builds the research database and owner review only. It does not enable a new sampling algorithm, synthesize audio, or approve any word or recording.
ownerTrainingContract.textBankFreeze: The owner requested this bank as the settled inventory for the next audio discussion on 2026-10-01. Freeze a versioned snapshot after British/Japanese review; freeze means selected scope, not independent pronunciation or audio approval. Corrections require an explicit new version.

evidencePolicy.stimulusMembership: Assign only when the actual word is visible in inspected primary study material. Record its original role (training, testing, familiarization) and population; do not generalize membership to our IPA or efficacy.
evidencePolicy.categoryEvidence: An L2 study may motivate categories without supplying our words, binary comparison, learner population or task. Those differences remain explicit.
evidencePolicy.editorialVocabulary: Proposed words remain proposals even when a dictionary URL is recorded. Unvisited lookup targets are not verification.
evidencePolicy.phonology: A descriptive inventory establishes language structure, not efficacy or difficulty for every L1.
evidencePolicy.rights: No research recordings are copied and no commercial reuse right is inferred from textual word-list access.
evidencePolicy.normalization: Lexemes are stored separately from category memberships and minimal-pair links. Context capacity checks require two distinct words per category and consistent target positions, but are not linguistic certification.
evidencePolicy.reviewIdentity: Changes to a word, IPA, meaning, dialect, category, context or attached evidence invalidate its previous review identity. Earlier fixed-pair notes remain on a separate preserved page.

methodFindings.finding: Japanese learners practiced identification of English r/l. Multiple-talker training generalized to new words and an unfamiliar talker; the single-talker experiment did not show that new-talker transfer.
methodFindings.limit: Supports attention to variability, not a universal optimal voice count or superiority of ABX.

methodFindings.source: Mora & Mora-Plaza (2019), Contributions of Cognitive Attention Control to L2 Speech Learning
methodFindings.finding: Categorical ABX assessed vowel perception using different speakers for A, B and X. X speakers were absent from training.
methodFindings.limit: Their illustrated X repeats one reference's lexical/nonword form. Our distinct-word X rule is an extension, not an exact replication of that assessment.

methodFindings.source: Cebrian et al. (2024), Differential effects of identification and discrimination training tasks
methodFindings.finding: Both identification and categorical same/different AX training improved L2 vowel perception, with retained gains after four months.
methodFindings.limit: AX is not ABX. Task-specific gains, stimulus choices and feedback differences prevent treating this as proof that our product method is best.

methodFindings.source: Shinohara & Iverson (2018), High variability identification and discrimination training for Japanese speakers learning English /r–l/
methodFindings.locator: Section 2.3.1, printed p.245; Results and Discussion
methodFindings.finding: Discrimination combined natural auditory (20%), processed auditory (40%) and distinct-word category oddity (40%) trials. Both regimens improved learning; identification had a larger early identification-test gain.
methodFindings.limit: One speaker per trial, varied across sessions; mixed tasks and a crossover design prevent attributing gains to cross-word oddity alone.

taskDefinitions.abx: Three auditory items: A and B provide contrasting references; judge which reference category X matches. The product uses distinct-word X and hidden text.
taskDefinitions.identification: One auditory item: assign it to a response category, which may be represented by a word, phoneme label or another learned cue. Written words are a design choice, not the definition of identification.
taskDefinitions.highVariability: Variation across words, phonetic contexts and speakers; compatible with different response tasks. It is not a synonym for identification or ABX.
taskDefinitions.evidenceBoundary: ABX is an established discrimination format, not the only standard phonetic-training procedure. Support for discrimination broadly does not establish that this exact product algorithm is superior.
